title: Thread Pool

validation.research: Six primary sources: Oracle ThreadPoolExecutor and Microsoft managed-thread-pool documentation; Brian Quinlan’s original PEP 3148; official Python concurrent.futures and threading documentation; original CPython 3.11 thread-executor source. Worker reuse, management of execution resources, fixed/adaptive ceilings, lazy creation, queue/rejection policy, shared state, thread-local cleanup, futures, outcome observation, dependency deadlock and shutdown are explicit. CPython 3.11 uses an unbounded SimpleQueue, so max_workers is not presented as a backlog limit. ThreadPool is a spelling alias; Executor and Worker Pool are broader terms, not exact aliases. Example and visual assignments are original teaching material rather than source quotations or a scheduling guarantee.

Instrumentation wraps actual executor, wait, file-open and task seams without replacing article scheduling. example_limits: Original Python 3.11+ real ThreadPoolExecutor inspector for a finite tuple of trusted Path values. Two lazily created reusable workers execute independent file reads; each task owns and closes its handle, retains at most nine sampled content bytes and rejects files longer than eight bytes. A positive coordinator window bounds submitted jobs awaiting collection, including terminal uncollected futures; FIRST_COMPLETED permits later results to free admission while an earlier job remains active. OSError/ValueError outcomes are reported per index and final sorting does not serialize execution. The finite input and report remain extra memory; the window is not a total-process memory bound. The pool context waits for submitted tasks and joins workers before returning, including on unexpected coordinator failure, so the demo removes its temporary directory afterward. Tests verify actual worker identity reuse, two-task execution ceiling, four-job window, completed-uncollected retention, running cancellation rejection, wait-timeout without cancellation, bounded sample sizes, empty/oversized/missing/directory paths, closed handles, all worker joins, and 256 additional inspections across windows one/two/four/seven. Assumes finite trusted input, stable file contents and operations that eventually return. No deadline, cancellation API, forced interruption, retry, durable jobs, general resource-failure recovery, task security isolation, rollback, filesystem snapshot, task affinity, fairness, completion ordering, or CPU-parallel speedup guarantee. A stuck task may hold shutdown open indefinitely, and shared-object mutation still needs synchronization.
